'''Dietrich Stauffer''' (6 February 1943 – 6 August 2019) was a German professor of [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Cologne]]. He is known in particular for his work on [[percolation theory]], [[cellular automaton|cellular automata]] and [[computational physics]].

==Life and work==
Stauffer was born in [[Bonn]] in 1943, one of the four children of theologian [[Ethelbert Stauffer]]. He studied [[physics]] in [[Munich]], gaining a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1970 with a thesis on [[phase transition]]s and the [[superfluidity]] of [[helium]].<ref name=DC>{{cite journal |last1=Chowdhury |first1=Debashish |date=2003 |title=Dietrich Stauffer: Unconventional in Science and Life |url=https://www.if.pw.edu.pl/~dynamics/data/stauffer_cv.pdf |journal=[[Physica Scripta]]|volume=T106|pages=7–8 }}</ref> He then did post-doctoral work in the United States on [[phase transitions]] and [[nucleation]] before returning to Germany to work with [[Kurt Binder]] at [[Saarland University]]. In 1975 he became eligible for a professorship on completion of his [[habilitation]]. Two years later he was appointed associate professor of theoretical physics at the University of Cologne, where he remained for the rest of his career.<ref name=DC/>

During the 1970s Stauffer carried out research on percolation theory, publishing a review in ''[[Physics Reports]]'' in 1979, followed by a book ''An introduction to percolation theory'' in 1985, which would become his most-cited work. An expanded version, co-authored with [[Amnon Aharony]], came out in 1992.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Redner |first1=Sidney |date=1993 |title=Introduction to percolation theory|url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article-abstract/46/4/64/407567/Introduction-to-Percolation-Theory|journal=[[Physics Today]]|volume=46|issue=4|pages=64}}</ref><ref name=DC/> In 1989 he was one of the founding directors of the supercomputer centre set up at the [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]], where one of his main areas of research was cellular automata.<ref name=DC/> In the 1990s he pioneered [[econophysics]] and [[Social physics|sociophysics]], publishing the book ''Evolution, Money, War and Computers'' with Brazilian colleagues.<ref name=Uni>{{cite web|url=https://www.thp.uni-koeln.de/stauffer/|title=Dietrich Stauffer|date=2008–2019|work=University of Cologne|access-date=31 October 2023}}</ref>

Stauffer published 620 articles and six books, as well as editing the ''Annual Reviews of Computational Physics'' and serving as a member of the editorial board of a number of journals.<ref name=Uni/><ref name=DC/> He was a visiting professor at several universities including [[St. Francis Xavier University]] in Canada, and universities in [[Niterói]], Brazil, and [[Paris]] and [[Marseille]] in France.<ref name=Uni/> Awards included the [[Gay-Lussac–Humboldt Prize]] (1992) and the Gentner-Kastler prize (1999).<ref name=Uni/> Following his retirement in 2008, Stauffer pursued an interest in history, attending lectures at the University of Cologne.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.philtrat.de/articles/1586/index.html|title="We are just tolerated people at the university"|date=December 2008|work=philtrat}}</ref> He died in August 2019.<ref name=Uni/>
